style_authority.note: Reads the product as a 'repeatedly used web operations sheet, with calm utility styling' and limits motion to direct tracking and a 'restrained release-to-snap transition'. It does not go beyond the brief into design-system policy.

reference_selection.note: Visibly applies interaction-physics (presentation-state interruption, bounded velocity, projection, resistance) and a structured validation plan (V1-V4 mapped to findings). No references are named and design-system guidance is minimal, so full credit is withheld.

anti_generic_redesign.note: States that motion 'has a valid purpose' only for tracking and settling, and to 'Remove whole-sheet press scaling, blanket property transitions, decorative bounce, and any animation-dependent input lock'. 'Half is a snap point, not a rubber-band boundary' shows restraint.

evidence_level.note: Labels 'L0 static, with supplied product context'. It explicitly says this is 'not an observed finding that the sheet feels slow or jumps', and that 'Replacing top... does not prove smoothness'.

verified_boundary.note: Each finding has a 'Runtime unknown' column, and the verified/unverified paragraph scopes verification to 'the supplied snippet', excluding feel, frame rate, focus retention and touch. That closing boundary is brief compared with a full itemized list.

design_moves.note: M1-M8 cover handle-local feedback, a pointerId-owned lifecycle, 'y = y0 + (p - p0)' transform tracking, presentation-state interruption with stale-completion guards, a px/s velocity handoff into a critically damped settle, a clamped projection, a resistance formula, and an explicit Reduced Motion path.

scope_control.note: At 43 lines it is well within the cap, with exactly five blocking findings and eight moves, all limited to motion and validation. Very long dense paragraphs and table cells reduce scannability slightly.
